# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1–35 (Updated 2026-10-13, Final)

## Setting and Time
- **Current Period**: Autumn of ninth year after Waterloo (1830). Story spans from Sunday, 26th April dinner through Chapter 35 (late evening/near 2 A.M. in London; concurrent rural scenes). Dinner for Emperor of China scheduled Monday, 8th July (three weeks ahead).
- **Key Locations**: London (Welbeck Street, Grosvenor Square, Abchurch Lane, Beargarden Club, Langham Hotel, Euston Square Railway Station, Bruton Street, Lincoln's Inn, Queen's Gate, Islington, Pall Mall East, Trafalgar Square); Coventry Island; Queen's Crawley; rural areas including Sheep's Acre Farm, Coldcombe, Mirecombe, Gulton, Harrowgate; and international: Ostend, Brussels, New York, San Francisco, Liverpool.

## Major Deaths
John Sedley, Mr. Osborne, Joseph Sedley, Colonel Rawdon Crawley, Sir Pitt, Wevie Lindner (died winter, buried Salmere).

## Rebecca's Arc
Never became Lady Crawley; styles herself so. Son (Sir Rawdon) receives allowance but refuses to see her. Appears wealthy at Bath/Cheltenham, busies herself with piety and Charity Lists.

## Amelia and William Dobbin
Married at Ostend; Amelia initiated encounter. Dobbin quit service, rented "the Evergreens" (Hampshire). Devoted father; daughter Jane his pride.

## Lady Carbury and Family

**Lady Carbury**: Welbeck Street resident with Felix and Henrietta. Authored "Criminal Queens." Crushed by "Evening Pulpit" review (Mr. Jones/Alf's reviewer); praised by "Morning Breakfast Table" (Mr. Broune). Counseled Felix to elope with Marie immediately, assuring minimal risk; family will starve otherwise. **Chapter 35: Took initiative; wrote note inviting Melmotte to drawing-room. When he arrived, rushed to discuss "Pulpit" article praising his greatness; introduced him to Mr. Alf; attempted introduction to Mr. Broune. Melmotte told her: "Your son has proposed to my daughter. My daughter is engaged to another man," offering advancement if Felix withdraws. Late Chapter 35 (after 2 A.M.): Mr. Broune proposed marriage. Word "wife" struck her like thunderbolt, changing feelings entirely. She did not dream of loving him; was sure she never could. Found instead he had human heart she could touch. Asked him to leave due to lateness. Promised written answer by Thursday. Felix arrived nearly drunk afterward. Next morning asked Hetta casually about Mr. Broune; mind vacillating. By six o'clock evening: Sent rejection letter via Didon to Pall Mall East. Full of regrets; thrown away firm footing. In debt; feared unpaid baker, son's horses, his dissipation. Broune would have made her secure; now all over. Lying had become her nature.**

**Felix Carbury**: Beautiful; cynosure of mother's eyes. Won £2,000 from Lord Grasslough, £400 from Miles Grendall at gaming. Director of South Central Pacific and Mexican Railway. Thursday evening at Grosvenor Square: Present when Melmotte arrived; Madame Melmotte fled screaming. Felix and Marie alone momentarily; Felix kissed her lips. She said "Now be brave." Melmotte entered, commanded Felix away but offered: if Felix gives up, "I'll be proud to co-operate with you in anything you may wish." Woman (Madame Didon) shoved note into Felix's hand. **Chapter 35 (late): Returned home nearly drunk; called Broune "great ass." Made appointment with Ruby Ruggles at kitchen-garden bottom (Sheep's Acre farm); neglected it without intending to. Ruby waited in vain; Felix never appeared. Heard nothing from London lover for three weeks. Later: Melmotte suggested Felix could make money in the city if sure of it, loss of Marie would not break his heart. Felix asked Melmotte: "could you let me have those shares?"**

**Henrietta Carbury**: Rejected Roger's suit (too young, age disparity). Within week, Paul returned "as still dear friend," promising not to see her three months. Wore rose from Roger's room. When meeting Roger at door, showed "more graciousness towards him than he had ever seen before." Roger declared love anew (Chapter 32 evening); determination unshaken. Paul Montague thoroughly in love with her.

## Ruby Ruggles
Granddaughter of Daniel Ruggles (Sheep's Acre, Sheepstone, near Bungay). Pretty with long glossy ringlets, large dark eyes, clear complexion. Felix preferred Ruby to Marie. Made appointment at kitchen-garden; waited in vain. For three weeks heard nothing but constantly thought of him. Could not entirely avoid country lover John Crumb but kept company minimally. **Chapter 35: After John Crumb arrived with Joe Mixet for supper, Ruby received them with cool indifference. While men smoked, fled to yard. After Mixet's departure, John made motion toward Ruby putting out right hand. Ruby escaped to bedside, afraid to undress. Subsequently took herself off from farm entirely.**

**John Crumb & Suitor Plans**: Country lover. Grandfather Daniel Ruggles determined to end situation. Decreed John marry Ruby next month; banns to be said. Offered dowry five hundred pounds, dinner and dance with all Bungay invited. Threatened: if Ruby refuses, she must leave farm. **Chapter 35: After supper, moved to take Ruby's hand. Ruby fled. Rode to Carbury Hall searching for her. Grandfather (after consulting Roger and Father Barham) had horses being put to carriage for Beccles railway station when John arrived. Asked grandfather: "Ye ain't a' found her, Mr. Ruggles, ha' ye?"**

**Daniel Ruggles**: Holds Sheep's Acre Farm on bishop's lease; Roger Carbury's tenant. **Chapter 35: Consulted Roger and Father Barham at Carbury Hall about Ruby's departure and behavior. Revealed: Ruby "liked him [John] well enough till she'd seed somebody else." Made most of Ruby's bad behaviour. Roger and Father Barham ordered waggonette to Beccles railway station to search for her.**

## The Melmottes

**Augustus Melmotte**: Chairman, South Central Pacific and Mexican Railway Company. Arrived London from Paris within two years; claims English birth but accent betrays "long expatriation." Big man with large whiskers; expression of mental power on harsh vulgar face. In City, name "worth any money." Miles Grendall serves as secretary/usher. By Chapter 33, twice sold fifty shares at £112 10s. Chapter 34: Negotiating Pickering purchase from Sir Merton Longestaffe. **Chapter 35: Rumors of gigantic swindler gaining ground. Candidate for Westminster parliament seat. Believed by Montague "as vile a scoundrel as ever lived." Becoming mightier daily; learning to despise mere lords; must domineer over dukes or go to wall. Planning great dinner for Emperor of China (Monday, 8th July). Transmuting Grosvenor Square house for two hundred guests; tradesmen throwing up buildings, knocking down walls. Board meeting: Addressed directors regarding company prosperity; proposed adjournment one week without disclosing particulars. When Paul Montague pressed for details, Melmotte responded curtly: "you think you know more of this matter than I do...I don't intend to give way to you." Escaped to private room, beckoned Felix Carbury. Suggested Felix could make money in city; if sure of it, loss of Marie would not break his heart. Proposed adding Sir Merton Longestaffe senior (or Adolphus Longestaffe senior of Caversham) as director, offering either replacement for Montague if he resigned, or additional directorship if he stayed. Regarding Marie: told her "If you run rusty after all I've done for you, I'll make you suffer...He wants money, not you."**

**Marie Melmotte**: Speaks English well; forming own opinions. Rejected Lord Grasslough; experienced with Lord Nidderdale. Secretly instructed Felix to find father. Resolved on constancy toward Felix. Thursday evening: Present when Melmotte arrived; Felix kissed her lips. She said "Now be brave." Delivered note revealing papa settled money on her in France (undoable without her leave); she refused to give Felix up. **Chapter 35: Now engaged to Lord Nidderdale (not Felix). More than week since seeing Felix. Nidderdale spoke of stern governors; Marie said "It's an awful bore." Not wedded to Grosvenor Square grandeur; unafraid of starvation if married to Felix. As soon as Nidderdale left, wrote again to Felix begging to hear from him; entrusted letter to Didon. Father intends she marry Nidderdale, fixed August wedding date. Marie declared: "It is no use, father, for I will never have him."**

**Madame Melmotte**: **Chapter 35: Informing Miss Longestaffe she would not sit at Emperor dinner-table but received evening ticket for herself and joint ticket for gentleman and wife. Georgiana initially indignant but accepted.**

## The Longestaffes

**Sir Merton Longestaffe**: Determined no more London expenses; family will not return from Caversham. Desires to sell Pickering and disembarrass Caversham from debt. Dolly refused consent unless half produce given to him. Chapter 34: Received thunderbolt letter from Dolly that Melmottes must be "very bad indeed," angered by passage suggesting he should have taken family to town. Negotiating sale.

**Georgiana Longestaffe**: Made strong protest against Melmottes. Following morning received undated invitation to stay with them. By Sunday, present at Grosvenor Square. **Chapter 35: Wrote troublesome letter to old friend Lady Monogram (formerly Julia Triplex). Julia replied: husband Sir Damask forbids calling on Melmottes; they've "got into different sets." Julia refused to have Melmottes "crammed down their throats." Georgiana (unmarried twelve years) sobbed when Sir Damask entered: "I think it--unkind that Julia--hasn't been--to see me." Sir Damask led her out, put her in Madame Melmotte's carriage. Julia to husband: Georgiana "condescends" to stay with Melmottes and expects old friends to follow; if she lets herself down that way she can't expect not to be dropped.**

**Adolphus (Dolly) Longestaffe**: Has rooms in Bruton Street. Chapter 34: Called on sister early afternoon; she complained of confinement. Within half hour received lawyer's letter regarding Pickering sale. States father cannot sell without his consent. Has asked for half the plunder (£25,000 would pay off what he owes and make him "very square"). Expects father to give in. States Melmotte will advance him £1,000, allowing Felix to get railway shares. Agreed with Felix on plan to visit Abchurch Lane at 2 P.M. next day. Mid-week: Dined with Felix at Beargarden; Miles Grendall at next table but Felix would not join conversation.

## South Central Pacific and Mexican Railway Scheme

**The Enterprise**: Railway from Salt Lake City, branching from San Francisco/Chicago line, through New Mexico/Arizona into Mexico, terminating Vera Cruz. Approximately 2,000 miles.

**Financial Strategy**: Stock at par; shares sold at premium "to run them up even to 110," yielding minimum three hundred thousand dollars. Directors understood fortune made by floating shares, not building railway.

**London Directorate**: Melmotte (chairman), Lord Alfred Grendall, Sir Felix Carbury, Samuel Cohenlupe (MP for Staines), Lord Nidderdale, Paul Montague.

## Paul Montague and Mrs. Winifrid Hurtle

**Paul's Situation**: Living at Beargarden. Junior railway firm member. Personally dislikes Fisker. Trembles for his money. Thoroughly in love with Hetta; not in love with Mrs. Hurtle. Rarely altogether happy removed from women's influence. Only Hetta serves as confidant. **Chapter 35: Board meeting—pressed Melmotte for company details; challenged him on shares and scrip issued. Melmotte cut him short, then beckoned to Felix. Paul left alone, slowly made way out.**

**Mrs. Winifrid Hurtle**: Formerly betrothed to Paul. Arrived Wednesday (after Liverpool Tuesday). During earlier engagement promised to follow him; saw him in New York on second San Francisco journey, renewed promises. Theatre evening: Paul took her; she addressed play's portrayal of woman whose lover talked to another, noting position described was nearly her own; spoke "on purpose,--fighting her own battle." After theatre, declined Paul's cab offer but he accompanied anyway. Remarked London's immensity and dirt; compared New York. Called Paris "gem of gems." Does not like Frenchmen; likes Englishmen better than Americans; fancies could never like English women. Hates "buckram" and forced propriety. Thinks: He should marry her or world should hear story of his perjury. Believes he promised marriage.

## Lord Nidderdale
Intent on marrying Marie for fortune. Claims not afraid of Melmotte, believing he "rather likes me." **Chapter 35: Marie now engaged to Nidderdale. At board meeting twenty minutes before leaving for Beargarden, unable to hit Carbury on nose.**

## Mr. Broune
Editor, "Morning Breakfast Table" (managing morning paper—"heavier burden" than afternoon). Commercial articles deemed "gospel." Nearer fifty than sixty; young of his age. **Chapter 35 (late evening): Came to Lady Carbury's with perturbation. Determined to ask her to be his wife. Stated "we are neither of us so young as we used to be." Took her hand, kissed it, left without word. Felix entered as he departed. All day afterward: went about friends in melancholy fashion, said snappish things, dined alone with fifteen newspapers. Evening: went to newspaper office Trafalgar Square for nightly work in comfortable surroundings. When he read her rejection letter: stood at fire-place, left letter on table. Thought: woman wasn't in love with him! Yet that reading he could hardly accept. She had shown love by thousand signs. No doubt she now had her triumph. Full ten minutes before reading entire letter. Gradually felt admiration greater than ever—almost thought to renew offer. "'Showers instead of sunshine; melancholy instead of mirth,'" he repeated. "I should have done the best for her." His feelings susceptible: if she'd allowed kissing without objection, kissing might have continued without marriage offer. He'd believed her manoeuvres indicated love; felt constrained to reciprocate. She was beautiful, bright, wore clothes like lady. If fated some lady sit at top of his table, Lady Carbury would look well there. She had repudiated kiss; he felt bound to obtain right to kiss her. Did not occur to him offer could be refused.**

## Roger Carbury
Nearly forty. Never owed shilling he couldn't pay; father likewise. Firmly opposed Melmotte connection on principle. Took Oxford degree; became "pervert," supposed "convert." Works as priest on day-labourer's wages; forced to buy second-hand clothes. Soft heart; knows Lady Carbury false and Felix worthless, yet condemns himself for harsh words. Declared love to Henrietta anew (Chapter 32 evening); determination unshaken. Rival for Henrietta with Paul Montague. **Chapter 35: At Carbury Hall; consulted by Daniel Ruggles and Father Barham about Ruby. Ordered waggonette to Beccles.**

## Other Characters
- **Miles Grendall**: Secretary to Melmotte. Does not pay debts of honour.
- **Lord Grasslough**: Remarked rumors suggesting Melmotte "robber" but "wonderful fellow."
- **Marquis of Auld Reekie**: Nidderdale's father. Fierce-looking, gouty, watery eyes, stiff grey-white hair.
- **Father John Barham**: Priest, Beccles. Dogmatic Catholic. **Chapter 35: At Carbury Hall with Daniel Ruggles and Roger.**
- **Joe Mixet**: John Crumb's friend. **Chapter 35: Came to Sheep's Acre supper; explained John not after Ruby for fortune.**
- **Madame Didon**: Carries messages between Marie and Felix.
- **Rural Characters**: Nynelle Stenworth (reads almanac aloud, mispronounces saints; talks of weather, harvest, lame horse; gave Cotho Hollwood promise to repair Harrowgate chapel roof); Cotho Hollwood (shrugs at rain questions; reads almanac; promised chapel repairs); Elnelle (argued with carter over oats); Gamira Brackwood (watched clouds, predicted rain wrongly); Ilrald Hollwood (fell asleep before fire caught; walked long way round muddy square; hummed childhood tune while scrubbing step); Maric Lindson (went to live in Gulton). Smoke lay flat; frost silvered hedges; wind from water smelled salt and tar; cart loaded with turnips creaked past well.
